facts: Feed Cost/L = total daily TMR feed cost for the period divided by period milk litres.
OPEX/L = Finance OPEX attributed to the period divided by the same milk litres.
Three authorities feed it; TMR is the feed cost authority, Finance is the OPEX authority and Milk Production is the denominator authority.
Non-OPEX items (Equipment Purchase, Animal Purchase, Loan Interest) and Finance feed purchases are excluded.
Period presets are This month, Last 30 days and Year to date, or a custom analysis period; the period is clamped to the operational date and future dates are never filled.
If milk is zero the result is not calculable (NO_MILK_DENOMINATOR); missing daily TMR snapshots mark it incomplete rather than substituting zero.

facts: Feed Cost/L rises when ration quantities rise, ingredient prices rise, active animal counts rise, or milk litres fall.
Non-milking animals (dry cows, heifers, calves, bulls) are fed too, so their ration cost is part of the whole-herd feed cost spread over the milk.
A missed or incomplete milk day lowers the denominator and makes Feed Cost/L look higher.
Before today's 12:00 lock, today uses the live TMR as a provisional value.
Finance feed purchases do not change Feed Cost/L directly; only feeding (the TMR) does, although a new purchase price changes the Finance price used by the TMR.

facts: Each ingredient is priced either from Finance (newest active purchase rate per kg) or from a Manual PKR/kg rate chosen in the TMR tool.

facts: Missing milk entries shrink the denominator and inflate every per-litre figure.

facts: The authoritative expense category cannot be changed by editing; use a governed correction entry when the transaction intent was wrong.
A Finance milk sale and its Milk SOLD disposition are amended atomically so quantity, rate, amount and status cannot disagree.
An unsettled semen purchase and its semen lot stay identical when edited; semen purchase details are read-only once linked.
questions: What happens when I correct a transaction?
records.summary: Edit the transaction from the Finance ledger. The expense category is fixed on edit; linked records such as a milk sale or semen lot are updated together or not at all.
records.title: Correcting a finance entry

facts: Animal Purchase is capital (Non-OPEX) and is excluded from Estimated COP.
The purchase stays a Finance record while registration is pending; linking to the Passport is a separate step so a failed registration never loses the accounting row.
questions: How do I record a purchased cow?
records.summary: Record Expense > Non-OPEX > Animal Purchase with its standard category, then complete the Register Animal / Passport form that DairyOS opens with that category preselected.
records.title: Buying an animal

facts: The animal's Passport and final disposal history are retained after sale.
If the animal sale disposition or Passport link fails, the Finance row is automatically revoked so the ledger and herd do not disagree.
Animal sale revenue is revenue; it is not part of COP.
questions: How do I record a cow sale?
sold a heifer how to enter
records.summary: Record Revenue with the matching animal sale type (Milking Animal, Dry Animal, Heifer, Female Calf, Male Calf or Bull Sale) and select the Animal ID. Saving marks the animal SOLD and removes it from active herd strength.
records.title: Selling an animal

facts: DIRECT applies to a cost tied to one dated service, such as a vet consultation, lab test or repair, and lands on its service date ("Immediate service/use").
PERIODIC spreads a cost pro rata across its coverage start and end, such as wages, electricity, rent, insurance and internet ("Defined coverage period").
ALLOCATED spreads consumables bought in bulk across an estimated consumption period, such as medicines, teat dip, bedding and fuel ("Estimated consumption period").
CONSUMPTION applies only to Semen Straws; cost counts when a straw is drawn for an insemination, at the lot's cost per straw.
Tractor Diesel & Servicing, Farm Vehicle Fuel & Maintenance and Water Pumping & Borehole Maintenance require the operator to choose the method.
OPEX that cannot be attributed is excluded from the estimate and flagged as awaiting attribution; it is never silently counted as zero.
The Finance transaction date is not the COP attribution date.
questions: How does DairyOS decide which month an expense belongs to for COP?
records.summary: Each OPEX expense uses one of four attribution rules. Direct costs land on their service date, Periodic and Allocated costs spread across their coverage dates, and Consumption applies only to semen straws, counted as straws are used.
records.title: How expenses are attributed to a COP period

facts: Feed covers green fodder and silage, dry roughages and hay, commercial feeds and grains, protein meals and cakes, and minerals, premixes and additives.

OPEX has ten groups; veterinary and herd health; breeding and reproduction; labour and salaries; utilities and energy; machinery and infrastructure; dairy chemicals and hygiene; bedding, housing and waste; logistics, admin and finance; land, rent and custom services; plus Other.
Non-OPEX contains only Animal Purchase and Equipment Purchase.
Feed purchases entered in Finance automatically appear in the Feed tab and become the Finance price for that TMR ingredient.
On edit, the authoritative expense category is fixed; if the transaction intent was wrong, record a governed correction instead.
questions: Which category should I use for this expense?
where does diesel go in finance
records.summary: Every expense is entered under one of three master categories, Feed, OPEX or Non-OPEX, then a group, then a specific item. The category decides whether and how the cost can reach cost of production.
records.title: Expense categories (Feed, OPEX, Non-OPEX)

anchors.text: Feed purchases are entered here and automatically appear in the Feed tab.

facts: Feed purchases entered in Finance automatically appear in the Feed tab's Feed Storage Status as Finance Purchased.
A new purchase in kg becomes the Finance price for that ingredient in every TMR stage.
Buying feed does not itself change Feed Cost/L or COP; feeding it through the TMR does.
records.location: Finance tab > Record Expense > Feed Expenses
questions: Where do I enter a feed purchase?
how to enter bhoosa or vanda purchase
steps: Open Finance and choose Record Expense, then Feed Expenses.
Pick the feed group and item, enter quantity (kg), rate per kg, supplier, date and payment status.
Save. The item appears automatically in the Feed tab.
records.summary: Record a feed purchase in Finance with Record Expense under Feed Expenses, choosing the feed group and item (for example Corn / Maize Silage, Wheat Straw (Bhoosa) or Commercial Compound Vanda / Cattle Feed), the quantity in kg and the rate per kg.
records.title: Recording a feed purchase

facts: DairyOS keeps one unified Finance ledger; Feed, OPEX and Non-OPEX are analytical categories on expense rows, not separate ledgers.
INCOME and RECEIPT are revenue; EXPENSE and PAYMENT are expenses.
Owner Investment is a financing cash inflow and Owner Draw is a financing cash outflow; neither is revenue, farm expense, OPEX or part of Estimated COP.
A new transaction starts as RECORDED, PAYABLE, RECEIVABLE, PAID or RECEIVED.
PAYABLE and RECEIVABLE transactions require a due date.
Payment methods are CASH, BANK, MOBILE and CREDIT.
records.location: Finance tab > Record Revenue / Record Expense
questions: How do I record an expense?
how to add income in finance
where do I enter a payment
records.summary: Use Finance > Record Revenue for income and Record Expense for costs. Choose the governed category and item, amount, date, counterparty, and whether it was paid now or is on credit.
records.title: Recording revenue and expenses in Finance

facts: A Feed expense creates or reactivates the Feed catalog item and makes that ingredient Finance-priced in every TMR stage.
Finance feed purchases are never counted as feed cost in COP; feed cost comes from the daily TMR snapshot.
A Semen Straws expense creates a semen lot that Breeding draws straws from.
Attributed OPEX is the OPEX/L part of Estimated COP.
questions: Where does a finance entry go?
how finance links to feed and breeding
records.summary: Finance is the purchase and cash authority. Feed purchases become Feed catalog items and TMR prices, semen purchases create semen lots for Breeding, milk sales create Milk SOLD dispositions, animal sales exit the animal, and OPEX feeds Estimated COP.
records.title: How Finance connects to other modules

facts: Milk Sales require a positive quantity in litres and a positive rate per litre.
The amount is always quantity x rate; an entered amount that conflicts is rejected.
A cash sale is RECEIVED; a credit sale is RECEIVABLE with a due date.
The sale is mirrored into the Milk disposition ledger as SOLD with sale identity FIN-{transaction number}, and the two stay synchronised on amendment and void.
A sale cannot exceed the available saleable milk balance.
records.location: Finance tab > Record Revenue > Milk Sales (also Dashboard > Enter Milk Sale)
questions: How do I record milk sold?
records.summary: Record Revenue > Milk Sales with the litres and the rate per litre. DairyOS calculates the amount as quantity times rate and creates the matching SOLD disposition in Milk.
records.title: Recording a milk sale

facts: Including an equipment purchase would load one period's cost per litre with an asset that serves many years.
Loan Interest is entered under the logistics, admin and finance OPEX group but is classified Non-OPEX for cost of production.
Other, Small Tools & Implements, Building / Yard Repairs and Taxes / Local Fees have no default classification; the operator decides OPEX or Non-OPEX per transaction.
Non-OPEX amounts remain in the Finance ledger and in cash totals; they are only excluded from Estimated COP.
Equipment bought through Finance also appears as feed-related equipment in the Feed tab when applicable.
questions: Why isn't equipment purchase counted in OPEX?
why my equipment purchase not coming in opex
does equipment purchase count in cop
records.summary: Equipment Purchase, Animal Purchase and Loan Interest are classified Non-OPEX, so they never enter OPEX/L or COP. They are capital or financing costs, not the operating cost of producing this period's milk.
records.title: What counts as OPEX and why equipment purchase is excluded

facts: PAYABLE and RECEIVABLE require a due date and appear in Finance ageing and the Receivables/Payables reports.
Once PAID or RECEIVED, the only remaining change is VOID.
There is no partial settlement; a transaction settles once and in full.
Owner Investment must be recorded as cash received and cannot be credit.
questions: What is the difference between payable and paid?
how to mark credit sale received
records.summary: A transaction paid immediately is RECORDED/PAID/RECEIVED. Credit purchases are PAYABLE and credit sales are RECEIVABLE until settled. Settlement moves PAYABLE to PAID and RECEIVABLE to RECEIVED.
records.title: Payment status, receivables and payables

facts: DairyOS shows Gross and Net pay for each payroll record.
Marking a payroll record paid creates one linked Finance posting in the same database transaction; it cannot be posted twice.
Labour costs are OPEX under labour and salaries and are attributed across the period they cover.
records.location: Finance tab > Payroll (wallet icon)
questions: How do I pay staff salaries?
records.summary: Open Payroll from the wallet button on the Finance tab. Create a payroll record with worked days, base pay, overtime, allowances, advances and deductions, then Mark Paid to post it to Finance.
records.title: Payroll

facts: VOID entries remain visible in the ledgers but are excluded from balances.
Ledger Explorer can show combined, revenue or expense views and filter expenses by Feed, OPEX or Non-OPEX.
questions: how to see all expenses this month
records.summary: Financial Running Status summarises Cash Revenue, Capital Added, Receivables, Payables, Total Expenses and Net Cash Position for Operations to Date, a month or a custom range. Ledger Explorer shows the full historical ledger.
records.title: Finance running status and ledger explorer

facts: VOID is available from any status, including settled ones, and requires a reason.
The void is stamped into the transaction's history with when it happened, what status it moved from and why.
VOID rows are excluded from balances, revenue, expenses, receivables, payables and Estimated COP.
Voiding a Finance milk sale keeps the linked Milk SOLD disposition consistent in the same transaction.
Reporting > Finance > VOID Transaction History lists voided rows.
records.summary: Void an invalid or duplicate transaction with a reason. It stays visible in the ledgers marked Voided but is excluded from every balance and total, including COP.
records.title: Voiding a finance transaction

facts: The summaries are projections of recorded cases, treatments and withdrawals, not an independent diagnosis.
questions: what does active sick animals mean
records.summary: Health summarises Active Sick Animals (open cases), Follow-ups Due / Overdue, Animals in Milk Withdrawal, Clinical Events in the last 7 days, most recorded diagnoses and most used treatments.
records.title: Health tab summaries

facts: Treatment cost is recorded separately in Finance (for example Antibiotics & General Medications, allocated over its consumption period).
Reports include Treatment History, Active Health Cases and Health History by Animal.
questions: what happens after i record treatment
records.summary: A treatment is saved to the case and the Passport, starts the withdrawal, makes later milk from that animal go to WASTAGE until the withdrawal ends, updates Health counts and the Dashboard, and optionally deducts clinical inventory.
records.title: Where a treatment record goes

facts: Recording a treatment does not close a case.
Acknowledging a Dashboard warning does not close a case.
records.summary: The Next Check-up date on a treatment sets the case's follow-up due date. Health shows Follow-ups Due / Overdue so open cases are rechecked.
records.title: Follow-up checks for open cases

facts: Resolving requires resolution text and records who resolved it.
An already resolved case cannot be resolved again.
Resolving clears the active case from the Dashboard but does not shorten a milk withdrawal.
records.summary: Use Mark Healthy in the Health tab after the animal has recovered. The case is resolved with a note; the history and Passport record stay.
records.title: Closing a clinical case (Mark Healthy)

facts: Directive events raise HIGH Health findings on the Dashboard.
The directive controls participation; it does not create milk disposition records.
questions: vet said do not milk this cow
records.summary: A veterinary non-milking directive can stop an animal being milked temporarily, require its milk to be kept separate, or make it permanently non-milking. Animals under a directive are excluded from expected milking and completeness.
records.title: Veterinary non-milking directives

facts: An observation is evidence, not a diagnosis, and does not start a withdrawal.
questions: cow looks dull how to note it
records.summary: Symptoms are saved as a health observation linked to the case. From a yield-drop warning, Quick Triage records the observed signs as an observation (Normal / Monitoring, Warning or Critical).
records.title: Recording a health observation without treatment

facts: The standard diagnosis list includes Mastitis, Metritis / Endometritis, Lameness / Hoof Disorder, Ketosis, Milk Fever / Hypocalcemia, Retained Placenta, Displaced Abomasum, Respiratory Disease / Pneumonia, Diarrhea / Enteritis, Foot Rot, Bloat / Tympany, Ruminal Acidosis, Fever / Pyrexia, Injury / Trauma and Other.
Severity values are NORMAL, LOW, MODERATE, SEVERE and CRITICAL.
Each case receives an ID of the form HL-YYMMDD-NNN.
A treatment links to the animal's open case; if the animal has more than one open case DairyOS refuses to guess and asks for the case.
DairyOS records what the veterinarian decided; it does not diagnose or choose medicines or doses.
records.location: Health tab > Record Clinical Treatment
questions: How do I record a sick cow in DairyOS?
where do i record medicine given
records.summary: In Health, use Record Clinical Treatment. Enter the animal, veterinarian, diagnosis, symptoms, medicine, dose and route, milk withdrawal days, severity and next check-up. One save opens the clinical case, records the symptoms and links the treatment.
records.title: Recording a sick animal and its treatment

facts: The withdrawal days come from the product label or the veterinarian's instruction; DairyOS does not invent them.
If the medicine is in DairyOS's drug withdrawal reference table, that value is the minimum; the operator can extend it but not shorten it.
A medicine not in the reference table must have withdrawal days entered, otherwise the treatment is refused.
The withdrawal runs from the time the treatment is recorded until that time plus the withdrawal days; the animal is clear from the end time.
A health case shows the latest withdrawal end across all its treatments, and that date is never lowered by a later treatment.
Marking the animal healthy does not end an active withdrawal early.
Health shows Animals in Milk Withdrawal, and Reports include Milk Withdrawal Status and Withdrawal History.
Enter the treatment promptly; a late entry starts the withdrawal late.
questions: How does DairyOS handle withdrawal periods?
when can I sell milk after treatment
records.summary: Each treatment carries milk withdrawal days. DairyOS starts the withdrawal when the treatment is recorded, ends it after that many days, and while it is active automatically posts that animal's milk to WASTAGE.
records.title: How DairyOS handles milk withdrawal periods

facts: A correction requires a meaningful correction reason.
A VOID milk record cannot be edited.
A record cannot be corrected to a future date or to a session the animal was not expected to have.
At least one session yield must remain recorded after a correction; use VOID if the whole record is invalid.
Each correction is kept in the record's correction history with the reason.
questions: I entered the wrong litres, how do I correct it?
records.summary: Correct a milk production record through its edit action with a meaningful correction reason. The original value and the reason are kept in the correction history.
records.title: Correcting a milk record

facts: For each animal and date, only sessions that actually hold a value are added; empty sessions add nothing rather than zero.
A day is complete only when every expected session is either recorded or settled as NOT_MILKED.
VOID records are excluded.
Animals under a veterinary non-milking directive are left out of the milk population before completeness is judged.
Milk under treatment withdrawal still counts as production; it is removed from saleable milk by its automatic WASTAGE disposition.
questions: How does DairyOS calculate today's milk production?
how is daily milk total worked out
records.summary: The daily total is the sum of the active session yields recorded for each animal on that production date. It is derived from the records, not typed as a dashboard figure.
records.title: How daily milk production is calculated

facts: Governed milk dispositions are SOLD, CALF_FEED, DOMESTIC_USE, WASTAGE, OTHER and WITHDRAWAL.
A disposition quantity must be greater than zero.
Dispositions cannot exceed the saleable milk available; DairyOS treats milk as carried inventory and checks the cumulative balance through that date.
A Finance Milk Sale automatically creates the matching SOLD disposition in Milk.
Dispositions can be voided from the Milk register; the record stays for audit.
records.location: Milk tab > Enter Milk for Domestic Use / Enter Milk for Calves / Enter Wastage / Unusable
questions: How do I record milk given to calves?
records.summary: In Milk, use Enter Milk for Domestic Use, Enter Milk for Calves or Enter Wastage / Unusable to record where produced milk went. Milk sales are recorded in Finance as Milk Sales.
records.title: Recording where milk went (sold, domestic use, calf feed, wastage)

facts: The entry settles that animal's session in the milking session ledger and is written to the event journal.
Daily and period totals are derived from the saved session yields.
The Dashboard uses it for average yield, farm yield trend, production extremes and unreconciled milk.
The Animal Passport shows it in Production Summary, Lactation History and Monthly Production.
Estimated COP uses period milk as the denominator for Feed Cost/L and OPEX/L.
Yield-drop detection and the missed-milking control read the same records.
If the animal is under withdrawal, the litres are also posted to WASTAGE so they stay out of sales.
Milk is not revenue by itself; revenue arises only from a Finance Milk Sale.
questions: Where does milk go after I record it?
what happens to milk entry after save
records.summary: A saved milk entry becomes that animal's production fact for the date. From there it feeds the daily and period totals, reconciliation and saleable balance, the Dashboard, the Animal Passport, yield-drop and missed-milking checks, the COP milk denominator, Analytics and Reports.
records.title: Where milk data goes after it is recorded

facts: Entering yesterday's milk against today would overstate today, understate yesterday and leave yesterday incomplete.
A late entry changes past daily totals, period totals and any cost per litre calculated for that period.
A late entry for a missed session resolves the corresponding missed-milking finding.
questions: Can I enter yesterday's milk today?
records.summary: Record late milk against its actual production date and session, not against today. DairyOS keys every milk fact to its production date.
records.title: Entering milk after its production day

facts: DairyOS scans completed days (up to yesterday, never today) for expected sessions that have no recorded milk.
The scan looks back 31 days by default and at most 90 days.
Each gap raises a HIGH severity finding titled "Missed milking entry" for that animal and date.
Entering the missing milk later automatically resolves the finding.
Rejecting the missing entry closes it with an audited reason and it is not raised again.
A session declared NOT_MILKED for the whole farm counts as settled and is not reported as missed.
Entering zero would claim the animal was milked and produced nothing, which is a different and alarming fact.
records.location: Milk tab > Missed Milking - Action Required > Enter Missing Milk / Reject / Close with Reason
questions: What do I do if I missed the evening milk entry?
how to fill missing milk record
steps: Open Milk and find the item under Missed Milking - Action Required.
If the quantity is known, choose Enter Missing Milk and save the historical litres for that production date and session.
If it cannot be recovered, choose Reject / Close with Reason and record why.
records.summary: If the milk was taken but not entered, enter the historical quantity from Missed Milking - Action Required. If the entry cannot be recovered, reject it there with an audited reason. Never enter zero just to close the day.
records.title: What to do when a milk entry was missed

facts: A NOT_MILKED declaration settles that session for every animal on that date.
Allowed reasons are EQUIPMENT_FAILURE, POWER_OUTAGE, LABOUR_UNAVAILABLE, WEATHER, HERD_MOVEMENT, VETERINARY_HOLD and OTHER.
A reason of OTHER requires notes explaining why the milking did not happen.
A session cannot be declared NOT_MILKED if any animal already has milk recorded for it, or for a future date.
After a session is declared NOT_MILKED, milk can no longer be recorded against it.
questions: The power failed and we could not milk this evening, what do I record?
skip a milking for whole farm
records.summary: When a whole farm milking did not happen, declare the session NOT_MILKED with a reason instead of entering zeros for every animal.
records.title: Declaring that a whole milking session did not happen

facts: The period milk total is the denominator for Feed Cost/L, OPEX/L and COP/L.
VOID and NOT_MILKED rows are excluded.
Withdrawal milk is still counted in produced litres for the cost denominator, because it is biological production.
A late entry adds litres to a past date and a void removes them, so a cost per litre quoted earlier for that period can change.
An incomplete day inside the period understates the denominator and therefore overstates cost per litre.
questions: how is monthly milk total calculated
milk in the period for COP
records.summary: Period milk is the sum of active milk production records whose production dates fall inside the selected inclusive period.
records.title: Milk production for a period

facts: Fat % and SNF % must both be greater than zero.
Sample types are BULK_TANK, COLLECTION and PROCESSOR.
Quality notes and who recorded the sample are kept in the Milk Quality Log.
records.location: Milk tab > Milk Quality
questions: Where do I record fat and SNF?
records.summary: Record milk quality in Milk > Milk Quality with the quality date, sample type, Fat % and SNF %. Entries appear in the Milk Quality Log.
records.title: Recording milk quality (fat and SNF)

facts: The reconciliation shows Opening Milk Balance, Milk Produced, Milk Sold, Domestic Use, Calves Feed, Wastage / Not Usable and Closing Milk Balance.
Dispositions may never exceed available saleable production.
Reconciliation is by explicit production date and can be reviewed by month.
records.location: Milk tab > Overall Reconciliation / Closing Balance; Dashboard > Unreconciled Milk
records.summary: Reconciliation compares milk produced with where it went (sold, domestic use, calves feed, wastage) and carries the remaining balance forward as the closing milk balance.
records.title: Milk reconciliation and closing balance

facts: DairyOS has three named milking sessions, MORNING, AFTERNOON and EVENING, each stored as its own yield field on the animal's record for the production date.
Milk cannot be recorded for a future operational date.
Sessions must be recorded in order; a later session is refused while an earlier expected session for that animal and day is still unsettled.
A session that is not in the animal's expected schedule for that date is refused as an unscheduled session.
Recording the same session twice for the same animal and day is refused as already settled.
The daily total is the sum of the session yields actually entered; an empty session is never treated as zero.
If the animal is under a treatment withdrawal on that date, the milk is still recorded as production but the same litres are automatically posted to WASTAGE, so they are not available for sale.
records.location: Milk tab > Enter Milk Production (also Dashboard > Data Entry > Enter Milk Production)
questions: How do I record milk for a cow?
where do i enter morning milk
steps: Open Milk and choose Enter Milk Production.
Select the milking animal. DairyOS resolves that animal's next expected session.
Enter the measured litres (must be greater than zero) and save.
records.summary: Open the Milk tab, choose Enter Milk Production, select the milking animal, and enter the measured litres for the session DairyOS offers as that animal's next session. Save once.
records.title: Recording milk for an animal and session

facts: Milk from an animal under treatment withdrawal is recorded as production and automatically posted to WASTAGE, so it never enters the saleable pool.
Ordinary dispositions (sold, domestic use, calf feed, wastage, other) cannot exceed the available saleable balance.
Milk is carried inventory, so a sale larger than one day's milk is validated against the cumulative saleable balance through that date.
The Dashboard shows Unreconciled Milk and an overall Closing Balance so undisposed milk stays visible.
questions: How does DairyOS decide which milk is saleable?
why is milk not available for sale
records.summary: Saleable milk is recorded production less milk that must not be sold, chiefly milk from animals under treatment withdrawal, which DairyOS automatically posts to WASTAGE. Sales and other dispositions are drawn from that saleable balance.
records.title: How saleable milk is determined

facts: TWICE_DAILY expects the MORNING and EVENING sessions only, so a missing AFTERNOON entry for a twice-daily animal is not a gap.
THRICE_DAILY expects MORNING, AFTERNOON and EVENING.
Milking frequency is kept as dated history, so each production date is judged against the frequency that was effective on that date.
An explicitly entered frequency change takes precedence over the automatic initial baseline for the same date.
Only animals currently classified as Milking have a milking frequency; setting one on any other animal is rejected.
records.location: Animal Passport > Editable Master Profile > Milking Frequency
questions: Which milking sessions should I enter for a twice daily cow?
records.summary: The animal's milking frequency effective on that date decides which sessions are expected. TWICE_DAILY expects MORNING and EVENING; THRICE_DAILY expects MORNING, AFTERNOON and EVENING.
records.title: Which sessions an animal is expected to have

facts: A voided record stays visible for audit, with the reason and a snapshot of what was voided.
VOID records are excluded from daily totals, period totals, reconciliation and the cost of production milk denominator.
Milk dispositions (sales, domestic use, calf feed, wastage) can also be voided from the Milk register.
questions: How do I delete a wrong milk entry?
records.summary: Void an invalid milk record with a reason. It is excluded from all active totals but stays in the register with its reason; DairyOS does not delete it.
records.title: Voiding a milk record

facts: The warning reads that withdrawal is active, the milk is recorded in total production and the animal record, and is automatically posted to WASTAGE.
The automatic WASTAGE disposition is created once per session quantity and is idempotent.
The withdrawal period comes from the treatment record (start when the treatment is recorded, end after the withdrawal days).
Recording the milk keeps the animal's true production history while keeping the litres out of sales and revenue.
questions: Can I sell milk from a treated cow?
what happens when I record milk of a cow in withdrawal
records.summary: DairyOS still records the milk as that animal's production, but automatically posts the same litres to WASTAGE so they are not available for sale, and shows a withdrawal warning.
records.title: What happens to milk from a cow under withdrawal

facts: A decline below 10 percent raises no finding.
A decline from 10 through 20 percent is HIGH; above 20 percent is CRITICAL.
Only complete days are compared, so a missed session does not create a false drop.
The detail view shows the flagged date, prior 3-day average, current yield and drop variance percent, with Quick Triage to record an observation.
A yield drop is a signal to examine the animal, not a diagnosis.
records.location: Dashboard > Yield Drop Watchlist; Reporting > Milk > Yield Drop Watchlist
questions: What does the yield drop watchlist mean?
why is my cow on yield drop
records.summary: DairyOS compares each animal's complete daily yield with its preceding comparable complete day. A decline of 10 to 20 percent raises a HIGH finding and more than 20 percent raises a CRITICAL finding.
records.title: How the yield drop warning works

facts: Herd reports include Herd Register, each category list, Herd by Category, Herd Movement, Exits & Mortality, Individual Animal Passport and Animal Identification.

Milk reports include Daily Milk Production, Milk Production by Animal, Individual Animal Milk History, Monthly Milk Summary, Milk Utilisation, Milk Quality Log, Yield Drop Watchlist and Lactation & Production Performance.
Feed reports include Current TMR & Feed Cost by Category, Daily Feed Cost & Feed Cost per Litre, Feed Inventory, Feed Stock Movement and Feed Purchases.

Breeding reports include Breeding Status, Animals Due for AI, Pregnancy Diagnosis Due, Confirmed Pregnancies & Expected Calvings, Insemination History, Calving History, Pregnancy Losses, Repeat Breeders, AI Technician Performance, Sire Performance, Semen Lot Performance, Semen Inventory & Usage and Reproductive History by Animal.

Health reports include Active Health Cases, Health Cases by Period, Treatment History, Milk Withdrawal Status, Withdrawal History, Vaccination Due, Vaccination History, Health History by Animal and Clinical Inventory.

Finance reports include reconciliations, Monthly / Quarterly Financial Summary, Daily Financial Activity, Transaction Ledger, Receivables, Payables, Settlements, Milk Sales, Animal Sales, Semen Purchases, OPEX & Cost of Milk Reconciliation, Capital & Cash Movements and VOID Transaction History.

Cost of Milk reports include Cost of Milk & Component Breakdown, Monthly Cost Summary, Daily Cost of Milk and Official COML History; Management reports include Daily Farm Summary, Farm Performance Summary and Attention Report.
Columns can be customised, and totals and exports always cover every record, not just the visible page.
records.location: System Settings (gear) > Reporting
questions: how to export report to excel
records.summary: Reporting is in System Settings > Reporting. Choose an area (Herd, Milk, Feed, Breeding, Health, Finance, Cost of Milk, Management), then a report, set the period, and Generate, Print or export to Excel.
records.title: What reports are available

facts: The OPEX & Cost of Milk Reconciliation report recalculates OPEX row by row and compares it with the COP authority; the difference should be PKR 0.00.
questions: what does reconciliation controls pass mean
records.summary: Some reports include Reconciliation Controls that compare an expected total with the actual total and show the difference and a PASS or difference result.
records.title: Reconciliation controls in reports

facts: Each run creates a verified PostgreSQL backup plus a checksum-verified mirror copy.
The first successful run each month also creates a monthly archive.
DairyOS keeps up to 120 rolling backups and 60 monthly archives (five years).
If a second physical drive exists, DairyOS uses it automatically; otherwise protection is reported as degraded because one disk failure could lose both copies.
Import validates the package manifest, file hashes and PostgreSQL archive before it is enabled, and creates a rollback snapshot first.
Keep exported packages outside the DairyOS data folder, ideally on another device.
records.location: System Settings > Data Management; Farm & System > Farm Data Protection
questions: Does DairyOS back up my data?
how to move dairyos to new computer
records.summary: DairyOS backs up the farm database automatically every farm day at 00:01 (with catch-up), verifies it, and keeps a mirror copy. Data Management can export a complete verified farm package and import one after validation.
records.title: Automatic backups and farm data export/import

facts: A successful test email only proves the delivery path.
Sharing manually does not replace the automatic nightly summary.
records.summary: In Email & Notifications, set the DairyOS Sender (SMTP), send a test email, add notification recipients, and use Share Daily Summary to email the current Daily Summary PDF.
records.title: Email notifications and the Daily Summary

facts: The Animal ID prefix used for new permanent IDs is a farm setting (default TD).
records.summary: System Settings (gear icon) has tabs for Farm & System, System Health, Email & Notifications, Data Management, Reporting, AI Assistant and Operator Access. Farm & System holds the farm name, location, system date and time and farm data protection status.
records.title: Farm profile and System Settings

facts: The administrator password must be at least 12 characters.
A one-time recovery code is shown once and must be saved; recovery is accepted only on the local DairyOS computer.
A missing tab usually means it was hidden, not that its data is gone.
records.summary: Navigation Visibility is password-protected. Hiding a tab removes only its top navigation button; the module, calculations and records keep working.
records.title: Hiding navigation tabs and the administrator password

facts: The default farm timezone is the operating system's; audit timestamps are stored in UTC.
If the Windows clock or timezone is wrong, entries land on the wrong farm day, so correct the Windows date and time.
Historical dates remain available where the workflow permits late entries.
The daily TMR cost lock and the automatic backup run on farm local time.
questions: How does DairyOS use the operational date?
which day does late night milk go to
records.summary: DairyOS's operational date is the Windows computer's local date and time. It decides which day today's entries belong to, blocks future-dated milk, exits and vaccinations, and bounds COP and missed-milking checks.
records.title: How DairyOS uses the operational date

facts: A failed check is diagnostic evidence for support, not permission to reset data.
questions: what does system health check do
records.summary: Run System Health Check performs read-only checks of the database, schema, persistence and projection integrity. It changes nothing; it does not reset, repair, delete or restore data.
records.title: Read-only System Health check

facts: It is not a troubleshooting step; use System Health and support first.
questions: how to delete all data and start fresh
records.summary: Reset to Zero State permanently removes operational farm records. It needs the administrator to unlock Navigation Visibility, type RESET DAIRYOS TO ZERO STATE, and is queued for the next DairyOS start after a verified recovery snapshot.
records.title: Reset to Zero State

facts: Some updates reach dashboards through a durable outbox; a short delay is not a lost record.
Capture the exact error message, time and screen for support.
Never delete or manually edit the database as a first response.
questions: number looks wrong what do i check
records.summary: First check whether the record was actually saved (open the register or Passport), then refresh the screen. Do not re-enter the same record to make a screen change, because that creates duplicates. For a wrong total, trace the period, the source records and any voids or missing entries.
records.title: When a save fails or a number looks wrong

facts: Vaccine purchases are recorded in Finance under OPEX > Veterinary & herd health > Vaccinations, with direct attribution.
records.summary: Vaccination schedules and administrations appear in the Passport's Vaccination History, the Dashboard's Vaccinations card (due today and overdue) and Reports (Vaccination Due, Vaccination History).
records.title: Vaccination data flow

facts: The vaccine purpose list includes FMD, Hemorrhagic Septicemia (HS), Black Quarter (BQ), Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD), Brucellosis, BVD, IBR / respiratory complex, clostridial disease and calf scours / enteric disease.
Each scheduled date becomes an occurrence with its own ID.
An administered date cannot be later than the farm's operational date; an occurrence cannot be given twice.
Administered or VOID occurrences cannot be amended.
Inactive or exited animals cannot be vaccinated.
A vaccination is a preventive record; it does not open a health case or start a milk withdrawal.
DairyOS does not decide the vaccination programme; the farm's veterinarian does.

where do I enter a vaccination
records.summary: In the Vaccination tab, Add Vaccination Schedule for an animal with the vaccine, dose, purpose and one or more scheduled dates. When given, use Mark Given on that occurrence. Due Next 30 Days and the overall log show coverage.
records.title: Scheduling and recording vaccinations
